column1: # tools/timing/cases/level2_binding.tsv -- the CPU-binding policy of every Level 2 application (hand-maintained).
# Tab-separated, "-" = empty. The engine (measure_level2.sh, default --bind-policy explicit) puts the policy
# into effect through the launcher's existing interface: HPCPERF_CPUS_PER_RANK=<cpus_per_rank> makes
# so every rank owns cpus_per_rank cores of the allocation's cpuset. The policy is application-specific and
# explicit: it states core counts per rank, names no socket or NUMA node and resolves no GPU topology (no automatic
# topology resolver, by decision 2026-10-02). Open MPI takes the cores in cpuset order; on the current machine that
# put the ranks on the GPU-local socket (verified 2026-09-30), which is a property of this allocation, not of the
# policy -- the record's placement block shows what was actually allowed anywhere.
#   launcher      mpirun: run.sh goes through hpcperf_mpi_launch.sh; direct: run.sh execs the program itself,
#                 nothing binds it (it stays unbound inside the cpuset, as in every earlier campaign)
#   host_threads  application host threads per rank beyond the CUDA runtime's helper threads: OMP_NUM_THREADS
#                 as run.sh sets it, or 1 for an application that runs one host thread (binding audit 2026-09-28,
#                 probe thread counts: 4 = main + cuda + cuda-EvtHandlr + 1)
#   cpus_per_rank cores bound per rank = host_threads (one core per host thread; no idle bound cores)
#   omp_pin       yes: OMP_NUM_THREADS=<host_threads> OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close are set too, so the
#                 OpenMP threads take one core each inside the bound set (verified on the current machine
#                 2026-09-30: hipBone's four threads on cores 16-19, one each, instead of five threads on core 16)
# --bind-policy runtime leaves the MPI runtime's default: Open MPI 5.0.10 binds a <= 2-rank job to ONE core,
# which is where the 17 mpirun-launched applications ran in the campaigns before 2026-09-30.
